history_note: Legacy directory names such as native-*, final, ok, readable, restored, and verified are not acceptance claims. Many native-* frames were rendered by Godot from native state.

cases.scope: Playable-character phone screen and native pause/settings menu

blockers: Menu typography remains a block-glyph approximation rather than the native phone display treatment.
Projected phone scale and composition are not established by an exact matched-state pair.
Screen-local illumination has contract proof but no accepted whole-sequence visual comparison.

cases.claim: Phone behavior is verified and its presentation contract is partial; visual acceptance is rejected.

blockers: Source-equivalent bitmap glyphs and selection geometry are present, but the composition remains small and weakly separated from the scene.
No exact matched-state C++ framebuffer exists to accept the complete overlay visually.
Foreground lawn geometry and dark scene compete with the overlay.

cases.claim: Restart behavior is verified and the overlay adapter is partial; visual acceptance is rejected.

cases.scope: Field daylight world visibility, materials, and composition

blockers: No exact native/Godot matched-state framebuffer pair exists.
The world remains sparse and visually flatter than later native renderer evidence.

cases.claim: Field lighting inputs are behavior-verified and partially adapted; visual acceptance is unverified.

cases.scope: Enemy surface cracking, damage response, digital blood, ingestion, and particles

blockers: Particle families still share simplified sphere-based Godot presentation.
Enemy cracking and translucency lack an exact native-renderer sequence comparison.
The selected frame proves rendering but not mature visual equivalence.

cases.claim: Combat state and damage contracts are verified; human and particle presentation is partial and visual acceptance is rejected.

blockers: No exact matched-state desktop framebuffer sequence exists for comparison.
The Godot Compatibility shader samples the current framebuffer rather than retaining the prior room framebuffer.
The maximum-strength frame is intentionally dark and requires a native matched-state reference before acceptance.

cases.claim: Door-transition behavior and the presentation contract are verified; visual acceptance remains unverified.

cases.scope: Native-owned pause and settings menu raster on the Godot phone screen

blockers: The frames are readable and the complete handset is visible, but no exact matched-state desktop framebuffer was produced.
Source Sans 3, centered composition, and unobstructed handset framing are inspected, but no exact matched-state desktop framebuffer exists.
Desktop per-glyph stencil reveal and paint splatter remain unsupported in this bounded slice.

cases.claim: Native menu behavior, Source Sans raster bytes, Godot texture upload, and inspected centered readability are verified; exact desktop appearance remains unverified.
